items.title: Russia releases American Stephen Hubbard from prison
items.feedTitle: Russia Releases American Stephen Hubbard From Prison, State Media Reports
items.summary: Russia has released U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard after more than four years in prison, according to state media. The release coincided with a visit by Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff to St. Petersburg for talks with Putin on Ukraine peace negotiations. Trump welcomed the release, which comes as his administration has taken several actions perceived as benefiting Moscow.

items.title: Putin agrees to resume trilateral Russia-Ukraine-US talks
items.feedTitle: Putin agrees to resume trilateral Russia-Ukraine-U.S. talks next month
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed "in principle" to resume trilateral peace talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the U.S. after November 10, according to Putin's foreign affairs adviser following a meeting with Trump envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. The announcement signals potential diplomatic movement on the conflict, though ongoing tensions persist between Trump and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy.

items.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump transgender inmate healthcare restrictions
items.feedTitle: Supreme Court rebuffs Trump administration restrictions on medical care for transgender inmates
items.summary: The Supreme Court refused to allow the Trump administration to immediately enforce new medical restrictions on healthcare for transgender people in federal prison. The decision leaves in place a lower-court block on the policy, preventing its implementation pending further litigation.

items.title: Chemical tank explosion in Ohio forces mass evacuations
items.feedTitle: A chemical tank explodes in Ohio, forcing evacuations and prompting fears of another blast
items.summary: A chemical tank explosion in Toledo, Ohio released glycidyl methacrylate into the air, forcing evacuations and prompting concerns about a potential second blast. The chemical can cause burning sensations in eyes, nose, mouth, and skin, with overexposure leading to headaches, dizziness, and nausea.

items.title: FAA certifies Boeing's 737 Max 10 for passenger service
items.feedTitle: FAA clears the way for airlines to put Boeing's long-delayed 737 Max 10 into service
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has cleared Boeing's 737 Max 10, the largest model in the 737 Max family, for passenger service after a nearly decade-long development process. The aircraft is designed to carry more passengers while using less fuel, addressing airline concerns about operating costs.

stlouis.title: Couple charged in shooting death of Missouri teen
stlouis.feedTitle: Husband and wife charged in shooting death of teen driving to St Louis Halloween party
stlouis.summary: A Texas couple has been charged in the shooting death of a Missouri high school student who was driving to a Halloween party near St. Louis. The victim was shot during what authorities are investigating as an apparent road-related incident, marking a tragic loss for the local community.

stlouis.title: St. Louis Public Library named 2026 Missouri Library of the Year
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis Public Library named 2026 Missouri Library of the Year
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis Public Library has been recognized as Missouri's Library of the Year for 2026, highlighting its community contributions and service excellence in the region.

stlouis.title: Missouri awards $9.1M for sewer district infrastructure upgrades
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri awards $9.1M to Metropolitan St. Louis Sewer District for wastewater upgrades
stlouis.summary: Missouri has awarded $9.1 million to the Metropolitan St. Louis Sewer District to support wastewater treatment infrastructure improvements and upgrades across the region.

items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the release of American Stephen Hubbard from prison while meeting Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg. The release occurred as the two discussed potential trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the U.S. to end the war, with Witkoff praising Putin as a "humanitarian" despite his status as wanted by the International Criminal Court.

Campaigners describe the measures as a "small-scale step" toward reform, though the bills face a likely veto from the country's president.

items.summary: Teachers, students, and civil servants have staged large demonstrations across Greece, including Athens, Thessaloniki, and other cities, protesting inadequate public education funding and calling for systemic reforms in the country's education system.

items.title: Indian court orders release of Cockroach movement protest leaders

items.feedTitle: India sees a drop in GHG emissions in 2025, even as UNEP flags huge gap in global reduction efforts
items.summary: India has recorded a decline in greenhouse gas emissions in 2025, even as the UN Environment Programme flags a massive gap in global emissions reduction efforts. The development positions India relatively favorably in climate discourse, though global targets remain far off.

items.title: Modi government intensifies crackdown on Gen Z street protests
items.feedTitle: Modi Seeks to Calm Allies by Shackling Gen Z Protests
items.summary: The Indian government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi is implementing stricter measures to suppress youth-led street protests, marking an unprecedented challenge to his administration. The crackdown reflects growing frustration with demonstrations that have shaken the political establishment more than any previous movement.

items.title: US Secretary of State Rubio meets Indian business leaders in Gujarat
items.feedTitle: Rubio meets Adani, Chandrasekaran; visits Reliance’s Jamnagar refinery
items.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has met with prominent Indian industrialists including Mukesh Ambani and visited Reliance's Jamnagar refinery as part of efforts to deepen energy and defense ties. The visit occurs amid ongoing U.S. focus on securing strategic partnerships and energy supplies.

items.title: India-US trade deal reportedly very close to finalization
items.feedTitle: India news: India-US trade deal 'pretty close,' says Trump
items.summary: President Trump has stated that an India-US trade deal is "pretty close" to completion, signaling imminent negotiations on bilateral commerce. The pending agreement could reshape trade relations between the two countries, though details remain limited.

immigration.title: Trump administration ends H-1B extension deference protections (proposed, not final)
immigration.feedTitle: Trump Administration Moves to End H-1B Extension Protections, Finalizes Restrictions on Work Permit Renewals
immigration.summary: The Trump administration has proposed to end the practice of "deference to prior approvals" for H-1B, L-1, and other employment-based visa extensions. Under the proposed rule (not yet finalized), USCIS would no longer automatically defer to previous approvals when adjudicating extension requests, potentially subjecting renewals to fresh scrutiny and potentially denying otherwise routine extensions.

immigration.title: Federal judge orders reinstatement of 2027 Green Card Lottery
immigration.feedTitle: Trump admin ordered to reinstate 2027 Green Card Lottery
immigration.summary: A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reinstate the 2027 Green Card Lottery after the administration attempted to suspend it. The ruling requires the State Department to reopen registration, representing a legal setback for immigration restrictions and preserving diversity visa pathways that the Trump administration sought to eliminate.

immigration.title: US visa revocations exceed 300,000 under Trump administration
immigration.feedTitle: Trump Visa Revocations Surge Past 300,000 as Crackdown Accelerates
immigration.summary: The U.S. State Department has announced that over 300,000 visas have been revoked during Trump's second term, marking an unprecedented pace of visa cancellations. The revocations are part of the administration's broader crackdown on immigration, with particular scrutiny applied to foreign pro-Palestinian activists and workers in certain sectors.

items.title: Wall Street gains as SpaceX lifts AI stocks, Nasdaq climbs
items.feedTitle: Wall Street gains ground after SpaceX helps lift AI stocks
items.summary: U.S. stock markets advanced with SpaceX posting strong earnings results, lifting AI-related stocks and driving Nasdaq gains. items.feedTitle: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion for Deceiving Users on Privacy
items.summary: A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for misleading users about its privacy and content policies in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The ruling represents one of the largest financial penalties ever imposed on a tech company and underscores ongoing legal liability for data privacy violations.

items.summary: India's Sensex and Nifty indices have declined for a second consecutive session as crude oil prices surged above $110 per barrel, weighing on market sentiment. items.summary: The FAA has certified Boeing's 737 Max 10, the largest aircraft in the 737 Max family, clearing the way for deliveries of over 1,555 ordered planes. cards.title: Identity precedes behavior
cards.insight: People are far more likely to sustain new behaviors when they tie them to a desired identity rather than relying on willpower or abstract goals. Reframing 'I should exercise' as 'I'm an active person' or 'I'm someone who prioritizes health' creates internal alignment that persists even when motivation wanes.
cards.takeaway: Next time you want to build a habit, define the identity first—then ask what that person would do in this situation.

cards.title: Friction breaks habits, ease sustains them
cards.insight: Most failed habit changes underestimate the role of friction. Removing one small obstacle (e.g., laying out workout clothes, putting water bottle by bed) often matters more than motivation. Conversely, adding friction to bad habits—like deleting apps or storing snacks out of sight—is more reliable than relying on self-control.
cards.takeaway: Audit your environment: reduce friction for habits you want and increase it for those you don't.

cards.title: Streaks work because they create social identity
cards.insight: Visible progress markers (calendars, apps, public commitments) work not because they track behavior but because they create a social identity you don't want to break. The 'chain' matters less than the story you tell yourself and others about being consistent.
cards.takeaway: Make your commitment visible to at least one other person; social accountability often outlasts personal motivation.

cards.title: Context resets override habit
cards.insight: People often underestimate how much habits are tied to physical context—location, time, people present. Moving to a new city or starting a new job can paradoxically reset bad habits because the environmental cues that triggered them are gone. New contexts also make it easier to build new habits with less resistance.
cards.takeaway: If changing a habit feels impossible, consider if a temporary or permanent context change might reset the slate and make adoption easier.

ai.title: Critical PHP vulnerability discovered by AI agents, causes internet panic
ai.feedTitle: PHP armageddon: OpenAI, Google’s Wiz find ancient holes, panicking the internet
ai.summary: OpenAI's AI models and Google's security tools discovered critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language underlying approximately 70% of the internet. The discovery has triggered emergency coordination among global cybersecurity agencies and software providers to patch the vulnerabilities before widespread exploitation.

ai.summary: Google Cloud has announced it will offer OpenAI's GPT models to customers, becoming the only major cloud provider offering all three major AI model families (OpenAI, Anthropic's Claude, and Google's Gemini). The expansion provides enterprises with consolidated access to competing AI platforms on a single cloud infrastructure.

ai.title: Anthropic proposes AI safety bill with automated killswitch mechanism
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
ai.summary: Anthropic has proposed legislation that would automatically pause AI models if they could potentially cause deaths to 50 or more people, establishing a safety threshold for model operation. The policy aims to provide automated protections against AI-driven harm, though critics question its practical implementation and whether it adequately addresses broader safety concerns.
